segments.say: [happy] Your first real paycheck...
will be almost eight hundred dollars smaller than you think.
[chuckle] School taught you photosynthesis...
[sarcastic] but never this.
So, little bro...
[happy] let me show you where that money goes.
[happy] Okay. Taxes are money you pay to the government...
out of what you earn,
and what you buy.
[narration] Quick note: this is education, not personal financial advice.
[happy] Say you land a job paying fifty thousand dollars a year.
That's about four thousand, one hundred sixty-six dollars a month.
[whispering] Now watch what happens.
[narration] Federal income tax takes about three hundred thirty.
Social Security, two fifty-eight.
Medicare, sixty.
[sarcastic] And your state grabs around one forty.
So out of four thousand, one sixty-six...
you actually take home about three thousand, three hundred seventy-eight.
[gasp] Seven hundred eighty-eight dollars... gone.
[angry] Every single month.
[happy] And it's not just your paycheck.
Buy a twenty-dollar hoodie with eight percent sales tax...
and you pay twenty-one sixty at the register.
[sarcastic] Now you're probably thinking: why would anyone agree to this?
[narration] Because that money builds the stuff you use every single day.
[happy] The roads you drive on. Your school. Firefighters, hospitals, parks...
even the clean water from your tap.
Nobody can afford a fire truck or a highway alone.
[happy] So millions of people chip in a little...
[surprised] and together, it adds up to nearly five trillion dollars a year in federal taxes.
[laugh] Think of it like a group project...
where everyone pays their share so the whole country actually works.
[whispering] Now here's the part that'll shock you.
[dramatic] At this pace, over a forty-year career...
you'd pay around three hundred seventy-eight thousand dollars in taxes.
[dramatic] Which brings up the real question.
[whispering] What happens if you just... don't pay?
[fear] Say you skip a one-thousand-dollar tax bill.
Penalties start stacking.
Interest kicks in.
[fear] And every month... that number keeps climbing.
[dramatic] And trust me... the penalties aren't even the scariest part.
[chuckle] That's what I'll show you in part two.
